subject: industrial_manufacturing_engineering

resources.title: NIST Manufacturing
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: Primary NIST manufacturing portal. Mappings use only exact ATLAS taxonomy keys and do not imply every linked item covers every mapped level.

resources.title: NIST Smart Manufacturing Systems Design and Analysis Program
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: NIST program for standards, protocols, cyber-physical manufacturing infrastructure, real-time control, analytics and enterprise-level smart manufacturing.

resources.title: NIST Manufacturing Systems Design and Analysis
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: NIST manufacturing systems design, analysis, modeling, investment and test-bed resources.

resources.title: NIST Systems Integration for Manufacturing
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: NIST manufacturing systems-integration work includes model-based manufacturing, industrial interoperability, digital twins and engineering information exchange.

resources.title: Methods and Tools for Performance Assurance of Smart Manufacturing Systems
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: NIST IR 8099 addresses design, operation, performance assessment, evaluation, analysis, decision making and control for smart manufacturing systems.

resources.title: Standards Landscape and Directions for Smart Manufacturing Systems
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: NIST review of standards across product, production-system and enterprise manufacturing lifecycles.

resources.title: DOE Advanced Materials and Manufacturing Technologies Office
resources.notes: DOE advanced materials and manufacturing program resources.

resources.title: MIT 2.008 Design and Manufacturing II
resources.notes: Modern manufacturing curriculum covering process physics, equipment/control, systems, design for manufacturing, quality, planning, cost, lean-system exercises, machining, joining, casting, forming and additive manufacturing. Labs are integral to the course.

resources.title: MIT 2.830J Control of Manufacturing Processes
resources.notes: Graduate course in statistical modeling and control of manufacturing processes, including SPC, designed experiments, yield modeling, optimization, adaptive/run-by-run control and real-time feedback control.

resources.title: MIT 2.852 Manufacturing Systems Analysis
resources.notes: Graduate manufacturing-systems analysis covering transfer lines, flexible manufacturing systems, throughput, work-in-process, scheduling, machine failures, setups and disruptions.

resources.title: MIT 2.854 Introduction to Manufacturing Systems
resources.notes: Graduate analysis of material and information flow, capacity, probability, inventory, queues, optimization, factory planning, scheduling, bottlenecks, buffers and batch sizes.

resources.title: NIOSH Elements of Ergonomics Programs
resources.provider: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health / CDC
resources.notes: Step-by-step ergonomics program guidance covering risk identification, worker training, controls, evaluation and workplace redesign. Mapped through undergraduate conceptual/application levels, not graduate or research specialization.

resources.title: MIT 16.852J Integrating the Lean Enterprise
resources.notes: Dedicated lean-enterprise curriculum addressing people, technology, process and management across product development, production and the extended supply chain; includes analysis tools and a team project.

resources.title: NIST Measurement Science for Additive Manufacturing Program
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: Measurement science for AM including material/part characterization, in-process sensing, process metrology, qualification, reference data, validation methods and digital implementation.

resources.title: Empowering Robotics in Manufacturing Through Metrology
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: NIST publication connecting manufacturing robotics performance challenges with measurement science, standards and metrology. It strengthens robotics/metrology evidence without implying hands-on robot-operation proficiency.

known_gaps: Foundation-level industrial/manufacturing engineering remains intentionally sparse; advanced or university resources are not down-mapped solely to raise coverage.
Ergonomics now has a practical NIOSH instructional progression, but dedicated graduate/research ergonomics curricula remain a genuine gap.
Lean manufacturing now has a dedicated MIT lean-enterprise course, while foundation/beginner lean instruction and dedicated research-level evidence remain targets.

Additive-manufacturing metrology and process-validation evidence is strengthened by the NIST measurement-science program, but practical qualification competence still requires projects and verification.
Manufacturing robotics/metrology evidence is strengthened by NIST; hands-on robotic cell integration and validation are not inferred from publications alone.
Research portals and graduate courses do not by themselves establish ATLAS expert readiness; runtime retrieval, practical verification, provenance and assessment are still required.
